A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FitControler and Fit4Men. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support matching content across substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Fit4Men experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 2, ablations, and generated-image results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds prompt-control comparisons, regular-fit subset results, and body-shape and continuous-control analyses.

M1.justification: The core architecture, losses, and training procedure are retained. Limited inference variants are added: using original DensePose representations for diverse body shapes in Section 6.5 and interpolating slim/loose fit-injector outputs for continuous control in S5.

E1.justification: Fit4Men coverage and VITON-HD/DressCode training remain unchanged. v2 adds qualitative DressCode evaluation, heavier-body test cases, and exploratory continuous-fit scenarios. DressCode was already used for training in v1, so it is not an entirely new dataset.

E2.justification: v2 substantially expands the evaluated alternatives to text-based fit control: a fine-tuned IDM-VTON+Prompt comparator in Table 6 and PromptDresser in Figure S3. PromptDresser was only discussed through citations in v1. The original backbone and condition-injection comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Existing splits, metrics, resolution, and training settings are retained. Added experiments introduce a 16,000-step prompt-baseline protocol using the proposed garment-agnostic representation, regular-fit subset evaluation, trouser metric sanity checks, and a continuous-interpolation sweep. These are additional protocols rather than revisions to the original benchmark.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial diagnostic evidence: text-conditioning controls, regular-fit-only analysis, lower-body metric validation, diverse-body/pose examples, and interpolation failure analysis. Original component and training ablations remain. The earlier standalone color-inconsistency case study is replaced by body-preservation and continuous-control failure examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands. The added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original ablation-table values are unchanged after matching renumbered tables. Substantial new results appear in Tables 1(b), 6, and S2 and the new comparison/failure figures. Some existing illustrations also change: Figure 6's slim-output Hu/Hd annotation changes from 0.25/2.41 to 0.33/1.41, without an explanation establishing a performance improvement.

T1.justification: S5 newly defines continuous-fit features through a weighted interpolation of loose and slim injector outputs. This is a limited mathematical addition for an exploratory procedure. The problem formulation, loss, and metric equations (1)-(10) remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central plug-in, dataset, metric, and efficiency claims are retained. v2 removes the introduction's explicit claim to be the first systematic investigation of fit-aware VTON and adds a conclusion-level qualification concerning insufficient body-shape diversity.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes color inconsistencies attributed to lighting and training-data bias. v2 replaces that explanation with substantive discussion of body-shape preservation failures, limited body diversity, and discontinuities under continuous control, explicitly identifying the method as designed for discrete fits. It also adds interpretations of regular-fit gains and the limitations of implicit text conditioning.

D1.justification: The abstract changes from promising a future code/data release to reporting release and providing a repository address; availability is asserted by the PDF, not independently verified. v2 also documents construction and training of the new prompt baseline. Existing hardware, optimizer, and staged-training details are retained.

R1.justification: The same 53 cited works are retained despite bibliographic reordering. Section 2 expands positioning against COTTON's length editing and PromptDresser's implicit text control, emphasizing explicit body-garment spatial alignment. The broad priority claim is also removed.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Fit4Men material moves from the experimental setup and Appendix C into a dedicated Section 5; ablations and appendix sections are reordered. Related-work and limitations passages receive localized rewrites, alongside author and front-matter edits.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout throughout. v1's Table 3 panels become separate tables, the dataset figure moves into the main text, and several comparison and failure displays are added or expanded. Figure 1 is rearranged and shortened; all nine original appendix result galleries are retained.

improvement.justification: The added text-control comparisons, regular-fit analysis, and explicit body-shape/interpolation failures provide useful evidence and clearer applicability limits, while the reported release improves access information. These gains strengthen an otherwise largely unchanged empirical contribution. Some new wording remains overstated: Table 6 favors prompt conditioning on paired short-sleeve SSIM and LPIPS despite its broad image-quality superiority claim.
